Row 4: Operational Execution Wins vs Headwinds & Call Q&A Forensic Audit

What Management Did Right (Operational Wins)

  • Operating Profit Inflection: Reached positive GAAP operating income of $207.0M (5.65% operating margin) a quarter ahead of plan, demonstrating high operational leverage on cluster deployments.
  • Power Footprint Acceleration: Energized over 200 MW in Q3 alone to surpass 1.70 GW of active deployed power, doubling operational capacity year-to-date.
  • Forward Pipeline Expansion: Expanded contracted power pipeline by >900 MW to over 4.6 GW across diversified global utility partners, including 1.3 GW international presence in Spain, India, and Indonesia.
  • Prepayment Liquidity Moat: Secured commitments for approximately $9.0B in customer cash prepayments and reservation deposits expected over the next 90 days, de-risking debt requirements.

Execution Challenges & Headwinds (Operational Drags)

  • Massive Cash Flow Burn: Capital expenditures reached $9,441.0M in Q3 ($23,558.0M for 9M 2026), generating negative true free cash flow of -$7,626.0M.
  • Substantial Financing Overhead: Net interest expense and financing charges drove GAAP net loss to -$709.0M (-$1.27 EPS) despite operating profitability.
  • Supply Chain Concentration: Heavy reliance on Nvidia Blackwell GPU delivery schedules exposes execution to packaging and foundry bottlenecks.
  • Power Grid Interconnection Delays: Local utility transmission queue constraints in secondary markets remain the primary bottleneck to accelerating energization beyond 2.0 GW.
Earnings Call Q&A Forensic Highlights (Hardest Analyst Questions)
Brad Zelnick (Deutsche Bank) — Blackwell B200 Cluster Ramp & Sovereign/Tier-1 Demand Durability

Question: Can you provide more granularity on the Blackwell B200 turn-up schedule for Q4 and into 1H 2027? Are enterprise customers and frontier AI labs signing multi-year commitments despite rapid chip architecture replacement cycles?

Executive Answer: Michael Intrator (CEO): 'Demand for our specialized AI cloud continues to accelerate faster than power can be energized. Every single Blackwell cluster scheduled for delivery over the next four quarters is already fully allocated under multi-year contract take-or-pay structures. Customers recognize that our software orchestration and networking fabric deliver up to 30% lower training latency than general-purpose hyperscalers, ensuring durable high utilization.'

Forensic Assessment: 100% CAPACITY COMMITTED UNDER TAKE-OR-PAY
Mark Murphy (JPMorgan) — Customer Prepayments & Capital Structure Self-Sufficiency

Question: You mentioned expecting approximately $9 billion in customer prepayments and deposits in the next three months. How does that cash inflow alter your debt issuance plans and equity dilution expectations for the $37B-$39B CapEx program?

Executive Answer: Michael Intrator (CEO): 'Customer prepayments represent the purest form of non-dilutive financing. These are enterprise customers and sovereign entities committing multi-billion dollar capital upfront to guarantee multi-gigawatt delivery. Combined with our operating cash flow inflection to nearly $2 billion this quarter, this liquidity provides immense balance sheet flexibility without requiring opportunistic equity dilution.'

Forensic Assessment: NON-DILUTIVE PREPAYMENT MOAT CONFIRMED
Keith Weiss (Morgan Stanley) — Adjusted Operating Margin Trajectory & Depreciation Headwinds

Question: You raised adjusted operating income guidance by 26% at the midpoint while operating margins reached double digits ahead of schedule. As $38B in assets hit the balance sheet, how should we think about gross margin sustainability against rising depreciation?

Executive Answer: Michael Intrator (CEO): 'Our gross margins in Q3 remained robust at 67.7% because cluster utilization ramped immediately upon energization. Because our contracts are structured with multi-year take-or-pay minimums, depreciation is matched against contractual revenue inflows from day one. We expect operating margin expansion to continue as corporate overhead scales over a doubling revenue base.'

Forensic Assessment: DEPRECIATION ABSORPTION PROTECTED BY CONTRACTS
